title: I almost didn’t make time to see it outside but I am SO glad I did! #...
transcript: This might be a hot take, but I actually enjoyed watching the Evita balcony outside more than I did watching it in the theater. And that's not to say that it doesn't play well in the theater, because I definitely think it does. But outside, it just feels like such an event. Like, you get there early, you're waiting around for her to come out, you're making conversation with the people around you, you're forming this little community, and then she finally comes out, and it's just mesmerizing, and we're all just staring up at her singing this song, and it's incredible. Inside, it felt like a very different experience because now you're watching it as an outside observer. And while I won't get too deep into spoilers, it was really cool to see how the crowd that came to watch her was filmed and integrated into the sequence. When you're watching it in the theater, it felt very different from, like, the walk in Sunset Boulevard, where, because he's walking through the streets, it felt like anything could happen, and the members of the public were more obstacles than anything. Here, though, it doesn't quite have that same sense of spontaneity because she is just on a balcony the whole time. But the crowd watching her actually became a part of the storytelling. It wasn't just an obstacle, but a visualization of her adoring fans. For anyone debating if you should go see the balcony outside, I would highly Recommend it. It is a very cool experience, even if it is very short. It's also a very different experience than you'll get actually watching it in the theater. Plus, you kind of get to make your West End debut.
